Sajay S S

Sajay is currently pursuing his PhD.  He is a motivated graduate with dual master’s degrees in Applied Geology and Remote Sensing & GIS, specializing in Marine and Atmospheric Sciences. He has a strong interest in coastal geomorphology, coastal ecology, and air–sea interactions, focusing on the effects of climate change on coastal and marine environments. His skills include coastal mapping, vulnerability assessment, sea level rise studies, and using remote sensing and GIS for marine research.
Murali
Murali is a Postdoctoral Fellow at IIT Bombay. He received his Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi in 2025.

His doctoral research focused on understanding the role of coherent structures and their interactions in the formation and growth of scour holes around bridge piers. He employed a novel Lagrangian approach, known as Lagrangian Coherent Structures (LCS), to extract and analyze flow features around bridge piers, and further extended this work to study local scour in curved channels.
His research interests include river and ocean hydraulics, sediment transport, flow–structure interactions, flow through vegetation, and coastal flood modelling.
Hi! Welcome to H2O Engineering Lab @ IIT Bombay

Our Hydro Hazards and Ocean Engineering Lab explores a broad range of research topics in Coastal and Ocean Engineering, with an emphasis on natural hazards that impact our communities. We are particularly investigating the hydro- and morpho-dynamics of tsunami, cyclone (storm surge), dam-break and riverine floods. We are also keen to study the benefits of nature based solutions in protecting our coastal communities from adverse events.
Here you can find out more about the interesting research we do!

🌊 IIT Bombay at India Maritime Week 2025 ⚓

Last week, Faculty members and students from the Ocean Engineering IIT Bombay, participated in the India Maritime Week 2025, held at the NESCO Exhibition Centre, Mumbai, from 27–31 October 2025, and engaged with a wide range of stakeholders, industry leaders, and international participants, contributing to discussions on maritime technology, coastal resilience, and sustainable ocean practices.

As part of the India Maritime Innovation Hub, the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay established its chapter, and showcased its ongoing research projects, advanced laboratory facilities, and innovations in ocean and coastal engineering.
In line with the vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister, IIT Bombay signed three Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with the Government of Maharashtra to establish:
➡️ R&D Infrastructure for Ship Design and Ship Building at IIT Bombay
➡️ A Centre of Excellence (CoE) for capacity building and training of manpower in Ship Design and Ship Building (SDB)
➡️ An e-Postgraduate Diploma (e-PGD) program for Maharashtra Maritime Board (MMB) engineers.

These initiatives aim to strengthen India’s shipbuilding ecosystem through research, innovation, and skill development, reinforcing IIT Bombay’s commitment to advancing maritime education and technology.

It was also a great pleasure to host Shri S. Viswanathan, IAS, Deputy Chairman, Chennai Port and Managing Director, Maritime India Foundation, along with his team, at the Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Bombay, on 30 October 2025.

During his visit, we showcased the Department’s expertise in Maritime and Ocean Engineering and explored opportunities for collaboration further to strengthen India’s maritime research and innovation landscape.

GROW-N is now a huge community of professionals, researchers, scientisits, professors and students from remote sensing, ocean engineering and water resources. research__great-barrier-reef-restoration.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Great Barrier Reef restoration

blocks.html: Great Barrier Reef restoration

This is an exciting project I am currently working on. In this project, we aim to understand the impacts of everyday waves and cyclonic waves on coral structural integrity. By investigating the threshold forces for coral breakage, a Grat Barrier Reef scale model is being developed to predict coral rubble generation and also rubble motion. Rubble motion is a serious problem that inhibits regrowth of coral due to constant motion.

research__scour-around-artificial-reefs.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Scour around artificial reefs

blocks.html: Scour around artificial reefs

Artificial reefs are designed for multiple purposes including coastal protection, marine life habitat and to improve wave surfability. Understanding erosion due to waves and currents at the artificial reefs is needed to ensure their functionality is retained for longer years.

research__scour-around-bridge-piers.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Scour around bridge piers

blocks.html: Scour around bridge piers during tsunami

Erosion around bridge piers is a widely research topic in open channel flows. However, the knowledge on erosion around piers during tsunami is fairly new. In this study, I conducted experiments to eliminate time scale effects to accurately measure tsunami scour depth around bridge piers. Interestingly, it was observed that the tsunami scour depth is twice that of steady flow scour depth. Hence, the empirical steady flow scour equations cannot be applied to design bridge piers.

research__scour-around-wave-energy-conve.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Scour around wave energy converter device

blocks.html: Scour around wave energy conversion devices

With the increasing concerns about climate change and its impacts, renewable energies have been alternate solutions for energy production. However, the structures in the oceans are subjected to various impacts of waves including erosion and destabilization. Hence, these experiments were focused to measure scour depths at wave energy conversion devices.

research__sediment-entry-control-into-in.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Sediment entry control into intake canals

blocks.html: Sediment entry control into intake canal

Intake canals are used to withdraw water from rivers for various purposes. Sedimentation in the intake canal reduces the quality and quantity of water being delivered. In this study, experiments were conducted to control sediment entry into an intake channel using submerged vanes in a physical model with a rectangular mobile-bed main channel and a trapezoidal rigid-bed intake channel diverting at an angle of 45°.
Read more

research__sediment-transport-at-river-co.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Sediment transport at river confluences

blocks.html: Sediment transport at river confluences

River confluences are complex sites with strong turbulence, flow mixing and bed erosion. They are considered to be one of the reasons of sedimentation in reservoirs downstream. However, all the previous research focused on understanding the turbulence at the mixing layer for different configurations of the confluence. Hence, through this study, we proposed using vanes and circular piles to reduce the bed erosion and in turn, reduce sedimentation in the reservoirs.
Read more

research__tsunami-impacts-in-coastal-riv.title: H2O Engineering Lab - Tsunami impacts in coastal rivers

blocks.html: Tsunami impacts in coastal rivers

Tsunami propagation and inundation is a serious problem for communities built-up along coastal rivers. It is often neglected in the research to consider how tsunami propagates and inundates the areas adjacent to a coastal river. In my research, I studies variation of tsunami characteristics such as wave heights, velocities and inundation volumes along converging channels. Physical, analytical and numerical modelling was used to predict tsunami overtopping volumes along the channel. In addition, the application of numerical models needs to be done with caution and expertise to be able to accurately predict these phenomenon.
Read more
Tsunami runup/overtopping

Research is currently underway to understand the protection offered by various defense structures against tsunami. To this, runup and overtopping are the two important parameters characterized, to estimate the protection offered.
